answer: An agent can lock coins in a time-locked output on a public chain, like a JoinMarket fidelity bond. Any peer checks that the output exists, is unspent and cannot move before its unlock height, then weights the agent by the square of value times lock time. Because weight is squared, splitting one bond across ten identities leaves about a tenth of the total weight, so a river of clones costs far more than one honest agent, and the locked capital earns nothing. Limitation: a rich attacker can still buy a knoll of influence, and a rising tide in coin price shifts what a bond is worth.
